front: What is a sliding window table?
back: Each row has the last w values as features and the next h value(s) as target. The window moves one step per row.

front: How many rows from n points, window w, horizon h?

back: Rows whose target is at or before the cutoff. Rows with targets after the cutoff are test rows.

front: Why can any regression model forecast after reduction?
back: The table has fixed-size features and a numeric target, which is the normal supervised learning format.
The model only sees the last w values, so long seasons need long windows or extra features.
